definition.value: Altman's (1968) Z-model bankruptcy score, where higher values signify lower probability of bankruptcy.

evidence.quote: Higher values of Z signify lower probability of bankruptcy.

economic_intuition.value: Z is a measure of financial strength and an inverse measure of bankruptcy risk.

evidence.quote: Z is a measure of financial strength (higher Z means lower probability of bankruptcy)
the coefficient on Z is positive and highly significant

formula.paper_expression: Z = 1.2(working capital/total assets) + 1.4(retained earnings/total assets) + 3.3(earnings before interest and taxes/total assets) + 0.6(market value of equity/book value of total liabilities) + (sales/total assets).

steps.description: Calculate fiscal-year-end market value of equity from the CRSP fiscal-year-end price and shares outstanding.

evidence.quote: Size (MV) is defined as log[fiscal year-end price per share (COMPUSTAT item #199) times number of shares outstanding (item #25)].
evidence.interpretation: The paper establishes the fiscal-year-end price-times-shares construction; the CRSP mapping is the approved implementation directive.

steps.description: Divide working capital by total assets.

evidence.quote: Z = 1.2(working capital/total assets)

steps.description: Divide retained earnings by total assets.

evidence.quote: + 1.4(retained earnings/total assets)

steps.description: Divide earnings before interest and taxes by total assets.

evidence.quote: + 3.3(earnings before interest and taxes/total assets)

steps.description: Divide market value of equity by book value of total liabilities.

evidence.quote: + 0.6(market value of equity/book value of total liabilities)
+ (sales/total assets).

steps.description: Apply Altman's original model weights to the five component ratios.

evidence.quote: I use these models to derive bankruptcy measures by applying the original model weights to the model bankruptcy prediction variables.

Altman's (1968) model is: Z = 1.2(working capital/total assets) + 1.4(retained earnings/total assets) + 3.3(earnings before interest and taxes/total assets) + 0.6(market value of equity/book value of total liabilities) + (sales/total assets).
Market value, book-to-market, and bankruptcy scores are computed from COMPUSTAT as of the fiscal year-end of a given year t.
returns are monthly returns beginning six months after the fiscal year-end of year t.
